reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Emergent laparoscopy for a ruptured ectopic in an Rh negative patient with ongoing hemorrhage (HR 122, BP 94/56, Hgb 11.9 to 9.6) and a full stomach (ate at 0130, vomited).

asa.rationale: Hemorrhagic shock from ruptured ectopic; emergency.

decision.rationale: Ongoing bleeding; delay increases risk. Resuscitate while inducing.

redFlags.evidence: HR 92 to 122, BP falling to 94/56, Hgb 11.9 to 9.6, lactate 2.6, fluid to Morison pouch.
redFlags.implication: Cardiovascular collapse at induction and with pneumoperitoneum.
redFlags.action: Blood in the room and checked, arterial line when feasible, hemodynamically stable induction (ketamine or etomidate, reduced dose), prepared vasopressors, surgeon scrubbed before induction.

redFlags.evidence: Sandwich and chips at 0130, vomited at 0230, opioids given, pregnant.
redFlags.action: RSI with cricoid per practice, suction, OG tube after intubation.

redFlags.finding: Rh negative, RhIG not yet given
redFlags.evidence: O negative; RhIG 300 mcg released to floor but not given.

redFlags.finding: Awareness risk with low anesthetic doses
redFlags.action: Amnestic plan, BIS or adequate MAC as BP allows.

planItems.item: Two large bore IVs, blood warmer, rapid infuser
RSI with ketamine or etomidate and rocuronium or succinylcholine
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Transfuse to hemodynamics and Hgb; 2 units available
